**What I found:** Move the billing rules out of `placeOrder` into a new `src/billing/index.js`, and have orders import it (the records call this BUILD and SPLIT). In the last 26 weeks there were 24 billing-rule commits, all editing `src/orders/index.js`. None of them shared a ticket with order work, and 3 of them broke order behaviour badly enough to need a fix the next day.

**Why it matters:** After the split, a weekly billing change edits only the billing file. Without it, a billing change carries order risk every week, at roughly one regression every two months. The split adds one module and one import. Nothing gets simpler structurally; that is the smallest cost that meets the requirement.

**Do this first:**
1. Create `src/billing/index.js` exporting a pure `invoiceFor(country, lines)`. Move `TAX_BP`, `DISCOUNT_TIERS`, the unknown-country check and the invoice-building code into it. `placeOrder` keeps the empty-lines check, calls `invoiceFor` and then `save`, so errors fire in the same order as today. Then run `npm test` without changing any assertion.
2. In the same PR, add the import rule "billing may import nothing outside billing". The repo has no linter, so this means adding ESLint and `eslint-plugin-boundaries` as dev dependencies, which is your decision.
3. On 2027-02-12, check the git log for any billing (`FIN`) commit that touched `src/orders/`.
